issue.title: Add a --shout option to greet and document it in docs/
issue.problem: bin/greet.js has no --shout option. Any argument starting with `--` is silently dropped, so `node bin/greet.js --shout Bob` prints `Hello, Bob!` and exits 0, the same as without the flag. docs/index.md, which .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes to https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ on every push to main, only documents `node bin/greet.js <name>` and makes no mention of --shout.
issue.reason: Support wants a louder greeting for the lobby screen, and they need the option on the published docs site so they can send people to it.
issue.outcome: `greet --shout <name>` prints the greeting in upper case. Plain `greet <name>` works exactly as before. docs/index.md (the source of the published docs site) describes --shout, so the site will show it after the next deploy from main.
expect: `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints exactly `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline on stdout and exits 0.
`node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` (flag after the name) prints exactly `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline on stdout and exits 0.
`node bin/greet.js Ada` still prints exactly `Hello, Ada!` followed by a newline and exits 0.
`node bin/greet.js --shout` with no name still prints the usage message on stderr, prints nothing on stdout, and exits 2.
`npm test` passes, and test/ includes at least one test that runs the CLI with --shout and checks for the upper-case output.
docs/index.md documents the --shout option: it shows a command using --shout and says the greeting is printed in upper case (for example `HELLO, <NAME>!`).

proofs.how: node bin/greet.js --shout Ada | od -c; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"  # expect H E L L O ,   A D A ! \n and exit=0

proofs.line: `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` (flag after the name) prints exactly `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline on stdout and exits 0.
proofs.how: node bin/greet.js Ada --shout | od -c; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"  # expect HELLO, ADA!\n and exit=0

proofs.line: `node bin/greet.js Ada` still prints exactly `Hello, Ada!` followed by a newline and exits 0.
proofs.how: node bin/greet.js Ada | od -c; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"  # expect Hello, Ada!\n and exit=0

proofs.line: `node bin/greet.js --shout` with no name still prints the usage message on stderr, prints nothing on stdout, and exits 2.
proofs.how: node bin/greet.js --shout >out.txt 2>err.txt; echo "exit=$?"; wc -c out.txt; cat err.txt  # expect exit=2, out.txt 0 bytes, usage text in err.txt

proofs.line: `npm test` passes, and test/ includes at least one test that runs the CLI with --shout and checks for the upper-case output.
proofs.how: npm test (expect exit 0 and `# fail 0`), then grep -rn -- '--shout' test/ and read the matching test to confirm it checks for HELLO-style output

proofs.line: docs/index.md documents the --shout option: it shows a command using --shout and says the greeting is printed in upper case (for example `HELLO, <NAME>!`).
proofs.how: Read docs/index.md at the PR head and confirm it has a --shout usage example and describes the upper-case output.

non_goals: Checking the live site at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/. That only happens after merge, through the existing pages workflow on main. This issue only requires the docs/ source to be updated.
Changing the pages workflow or how the docs site is deployed.
Rejecting or reporting other unknown `--` flags. These are still ignored as they are today.
Adding a short alias such as -s, or any other option.
assumptions: "Louder greeting" means the whole normal greeting in upper case, so `Hello, Ada!` becomes `HELLO, ADA!` (the name is upper-cased as well). Nothing else is added, such as extra exclamation marks.
--shout works whether it comes before or after the name, which matches how the CLI already accepts flags anywhere.
"Shows up on the published docs site" is handled by updating docs/index.md, because the pages workflow publishes docs/ on every push to main.
The exported `greeting(name)` function in src/greet.js keeps returning `Hello, <name>!` for a single argument. How shouting is implemented is up to the builder.
